--- title: "Wedge-tailed eagle behavioural classification" subtitle: "Agreement between methods" author: - name: "Scott Forrest" url: https://swforrest.github.io/ orcid: 0000-0001-9529-0108 affiliation: University of Tasmania, QUT email: "scottwforrest@gmail.com" - name: "James Pay" affiliation: University of Tasmania date: "2026-11-25" execute: cache: false warning: false bibliography: references.bib toc: true number-sections: false format: html: # self-contained: true code-fold: true code-summary: "Show code" code-tools: true df-print: paged code-line-numbers: true code-overflow: scroll fig-format: png fig-dpi: 150 editor: source editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline abstract: | Compare the state classifications based on k-means with different input variables, hidden Markov models (HMMs), and expectation-maximisation binary clustering (EMbC). --- # Load packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) packages <- c("leaflet") walk(packages, require, character.only = T) ``` ::: # Choose the methods to compare Set a method to `FALSE` to leave it out of the agreement and consensus (and all of the plots below). Nothing else in the notebook needs to change - the agreement categories and the majority needed for a consensus are worked out from the number of methods that are included. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # the classification methods - TRUE to include, FALSE to leave out include_methods <- c(kmeans_inst = TRUE, kmeans_agg = TRUE, kmeans_comb = TRUE, hmm = TRUE, embc = TRUE) # the names of the state columns of the included methods state_cols <- names(include_methods)[include_methods] # the number of methods, and how many need to agree for a majority (more than half) n_methods <- length(state_cols) n_majority <- floor(n_methods / 2) + 1 n_methods ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} n_majority ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: # Import data from the model outputs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # the eagle to compare the methods for eagle_name <- "Tabatha" kmeans_instantaneous <- read_csv(paste0("outputs/eagle_states_kmeans_instantaneous_", eagle_name, ".csv")) kmeans_aggregated <- read_csv(paste0("outputs/eagle_states_kmeans_aggregated_", eagle_name, ".csv")) kmeans_combined <- read_csv(paste0("outputs/eagle_states_kmeans_combined_", eagle_name, ".csv")) hmm <- read_csv(paste0("outputs/eagle_states_hmm_", eagle_name, ".csv")) embc <- read_csv(paste0("outputs/eagle_states_embc_aggregated_", eagle_name, ".csv")) ``` ::: ## Join the dataframes The dataframes have different numbers of rows, as some variables had NAs in some of the scripts but not others. We join them by the eagle's name and the start time of each step, and then only keep the fixes that were classified by all of the included methods. We keep the location and flight variables from the k-means combined data, and only the behaviours from the others (plus the probability of the most likely state from the 3-state HMM). The behaviours are labelled in each classification script and saved in the `behavior` column - from the 3-cluster k-means models, the 3-state HMM and the smoothed EMbC behaviours. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # number of rows in each dataframe tibble(data = c("kmeans_instantaneous", "kmeans_aggregated", "kmeans_combined", "hmm", "embc"), rows = c(nrow(kmeans_instantaneous), nrow(kmeans_aggregated), nrow(kmeans_combined), nrow(hmm), nrow(embc))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} eagle_states <- kmeans_combined %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, stepend_dtime, stepend_utme, stepend_utmn, flight_n, lat, lon, F_AOG, F_Sn, F_Vrate, F_radians, F_radians_abs, F_turn_cum_window, F_speed_mean_window, F_Vrate_mean_window, kmeans_comb = behavior) %>% full_join(kmeans_aggregated %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, kmeans_agg = behavior), by = c("name", "stepstart_dtime")) %>% full_join(kmeans_instantaneous %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, kmeans_inst = behavior), by = c("name", "stepstart_dtime")) %>% full_join(hmm %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, hmm = behavior, hmm3_prob), by = c("name", "stepstart_dtime")) %>% full_join(embc %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, embc = behavior), by = c("name", "stepstart_dtime")) # number of rows after joining nrow(eagle_states) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 773875 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # drop rows that are missing a state from any of the included methods, or the # locations (which come from the k-means combined data) eagle_states <- eagle_states %>% drop_na(all_of(state_cols), lat, lon) # number of rows that were classified by all of the included methods nrow(eagle_states) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 773324 ``` ::: ::: ## Labels and colours The cluster (k-means) and state (HMM) numbers are arbitrary, so state 1 in one method isn't necessarily state 1 in another. The behaviours are therefore labelled in each of the classification scripts (where the clusters and states can be checked against the flight variables), and we use those labels here. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # labels to use in the plots method_labels <- c(kmeans_inst = "K-means instantaneous", kmeans_agg = "K-means aggregated", kmeans_comb = "K-means combined", hmm = "HMM instantaneous", embc = "EMbC aggregated") # only keep the labels of the included methods method_labels <- method_labels[state_cols] # colours that are used in all of the plots and the map state_colours <- c(ascending = "#E69F00", flapping = "#56B4E9", gliding = "#009E73") # the consensus state can also be 'no majority' (when no state has a majority) # consensus_colours <- c(state_colours, "no majority" = "#999999") consensus_colours <- c(state_colours, "no majority" = "red") # the agreement categories go from all of the methods agreeing down to a bare # majority, and then 'no majority' (e.g. with 5 methods: "5 of 5 agree", # "4 of 5 agree", "3 of 5 agree", "no majority"). The colours go from dark # blue to yellow, with orange for no majority agreement_colours <- c(colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "#56B4E9", "#F0E442"))(n_methods - n_majority + 1), "#D55E00") names(agreement_colours) <- c(paste(n_methods:n_majority, "of", n_methods, "agree"), "no majority") agreement_colours ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 5 of 5 agree 4 of 5 agree 3 of 5 agree no majority "#0072B2" "#56B4E9" "#F0E442" "#D55E00" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # use the same factor levels for every method (so the colours are consistent) eagle_states <- eagle_states %>% mutate(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) factor(x, levels = names(state_colours)))) ``` ::: ## Calculate the agreement between the methods For each fix we count how many of the included methods classified it as each state. From this we get: - `n_agree` - the number of methods that agree on the most common state - `agreement` - how many of the methods agree (e.g. 4 of 5), or 'no majority' when no state was classified by more than half of the methods - `consensus` - the state that more than half of the methods agree on (otherwise 'no majority') ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} eagle_states <- eagle_states %>% mutate( # the number of methods that classified each fix as each state n_ascending = rowSums(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) x == "ascending")), n_flapping = rowSums(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) x == "flapping")), n_gliding = rowSums(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) x == "gliding")), # the number of methods that agree on the most common state n_agree = pmax(n_ascending, n_flapping, n_gliding), # e.g. "4 of 5 agree", or 'no majority' if fewer than n_majority methods agree agreement = if_else(n_agree >= n_majority, paste(n_agree, "of", n_methods, "agree"), "no majority"), # the state that a majority of the methods agree on (only one state can # have a majority, as it's more than half of the methods) consensus = case_when(n_ascending >= n_majority ~ "ascending", n_flapping >= n_majority ~ "flapping", n_gliding >= n_majority ~ "gliding", TRUE ~ "no majority") ) %>% # set the order of the levels for plotting mutate(agreement = factor(agreement, levels = names(agreement_colours)), consensus = factor(consensus, levels = names(consensus_colours))) ``` ::: We also create a 'long' version of the data, with one row for each fix and method, which is easier to plot. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} eagle_states_long <- eagle_states %>% select(stepstart_dtime, all_of(state_cols), n_ascending, n_flapping, n_gliding, n_agree, consensus) %>% pivot_longer(all_of(state_cols), names_to = "method", values_to = "state") %>% mutate(method = factor(method_labels[method], levels = method_labels), # how many of the OTHER methods agree with this method's state n_others_agree = case_when(state == "ascending" ~ n_ascending - 1, state == "flapping" ~ n_flapping - 1, state == "gliding" ~ n_gliding - 1)) ``` ::: # State proportions for each method Before looking at agreement at each fix, how often does each method classify each state overall? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states_long, aes(x = method, fill = state)) + geom_bar(position = "fill") + scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours) + # wrap the method names so they don't overlap scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(12)) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion of fixes", fill = "State") + theme_bw() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png) ::: ::: # Pairwise agreement ## Agreement between each pair of methods The percentage of fixes where each pair of methods classified the same state, and Cohen's kappa, which accounts for the agreement that would be expected by chance given how often each method classifies each state (1 = perfect agreement, 0 = no better than chance). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # all pairs of methods method_pairs <- combn(state_cols, 2, simplify = FALSE) pairwise_agreement <- map(method_pairs, \(pair) { state_a <- eagle_states[[pair[1]]] state_b <- eagle_states[[pair[2]]] # proportion of fixes where both methods classified the same state p_observed <- mean(state_a == state_b) # agreement expected by chance, from the proportions of each state in each method p_chance <- sum(prop.table(table(state_a)) * prop.table(table(state_b))) tibble(method_a = method_labels[pair[1]], method_b = method_labels[pair[2]], agreement = p_observed, kappa = (p_observed - p_chance) / (1 - p_chance)) }) %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(method_a = factor(method_a, levels = method_labels), method_b = factor(method_b, levels = method_labels)) pairwise_agreement ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(pairwise_agreement, aes(x = method_b, y = method_a, fill = agreement)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(agreement * 100), "%\nkappa = ", round(kappa, 2)))) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#0072B2", limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) + # put the first method at the top scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Agreement") + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png) ::: ::: ## Cross-tabulation of the states for each pair of methods The proportion of all fixes with each combination of states, for each pair of methods. The rows are the states from the method on the right and the columns are the states from the method at the top. The diagonal (top left to bottom right) is where the two methods agree, and the off-diagonals show which states are confused with each other. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairwise_tables <- map(method_pairs, \(pair) { eagle_states %>% count(state_a = .data[[pair[1]]], state_b = .data[[pair[2]]]) %>% mutate(prop = n / sum(n), method_a = method_labels[pair[1]], method_b = method_labels[pair[2]]) }) %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(method_a = factor(method_a, levels = method_labels), method_b = factor(method_b, levels = method_labels)) ggplot(pairwise_tables, aes(x = state_b, y = state_a, fill = prop)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1))) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#0072B2", labels = scales::percent) + # put ascending at the top so the diagonal is where the methods agree scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) + facet_grid(method_a ~ method_b) + labs(x = "State (method at the top)", y = "State (method on the right)", fill = "Proportion\nof fixes") + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png) ::: ::: # Agreement between all of the methods ## How often do the methods agree? The bars are coloured by the consensus state (the state that more than half of the methods agree on). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # proportion of fixes in each agreement category eagle_states %>% count(agreement) %>% mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states, aes(x = agreement, fill = consensus)) + geom_bar() + scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of fixes", fill = "Consensus state") + theme_bw() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png) ::: ::: ## Agreement for each method and state When a method classifies a fix as a particular state, how many of the other methods agree with it? States where most of the other methods agree (dark) are consistently identified, regardless of the method. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states_long, aes(x = state, fill = factor(n_others_agree))) + geom_bar(position = "fill") + scale_fill_viridis_d(direction = -1) + facet_wrap(~ method, nrow = 1) + labs(x = "State classified by the method", y = "Proportion of fixes", fill = "Number of other\nmethods that agree") + theme_bw() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png) ::: ::: ## Which method is the odd one out? When all but one of the methods agree, which method disagrees? The bars are coloured by the state that the other methods agreed on. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} eagle_states_long %>% # the fixes where all but one of the methods agree, and the method that # disagrees (as characters, as the factor levels differ) filter(n_agree == n_methods - 1, as.character(state) != as.character(consensus)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = method, fill = consensus)) + geom_bar() + scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) + # wrap the method names so they don't overlap scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(12)) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + labs(x = "Method that disagrees", y = "Number of fixes", fill = "State the other\nmethods agree on") + theme_bw() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png) ::: ::: # What do the fixes with no majority look like? The flight variables for each consensus state. Fixes with no majority are those where the methods disagree, and are likely to be in between the other behaviours (or at transitions between them). We remove outliers for clarity and faster plotting. ::: {.panel-tabset} ## Altitude above ground ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states, aes(x = consensus, y = F_AOG, fill = consensus)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1000)) + labs(x = "Consensus state", y = "Altitude above ground (m)") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png) ::: ::: ## Absolute turn angle ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states, aes(x = consensus, y = F_radians_abs, fill = consensus)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Consensus state", y = "Absolute turn angle (radians)") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png) ::: ::: ## Speed over ground ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states, aes(x = consensus, y = F_Sn, fill = consensus)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 25)) + labs(x = "Consensus state", y = "Speed (m/s)") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png) ::: ::: ## Vertical rate ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states, aes(x = consensus, y = F_Vrate, fill = consensus)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5, 5)) + labs(x = "Consensus state", y = "Vertical rate (m/s)") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png) ::: ::: ::: ## Agreement and the certainty of the HMM The HMM gives the probability of the most likely state at each fix (`hmm3_prob`). Do the methods disagree more where the HMM is less certain? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(eagle_states, aes(x = agreement, y = hmm3_prob, fill = agreement)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + scale_fill_manual(values = agreement_colours) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0,1,0.1)) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Probability of the most likely HMM state") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png) ::: ::: # Agreement through a flight segment Choose a flight segment to explore, and look at the states from each method through time, along with the flight variables. The segment is chosen to be the one closest to *n* fixes, but you can change it to any other flight segment by changing `flight_n_explore` below. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flight_length <- 1500 # in number of locations # choose a flight segment - here the one closest to n locations # (replace flight_n_explore with any other flight_n to explore a different flight) flight_counts <- eagle_states %>% count(flight_n) flight_n_explore <- flight_counts$flight_n[which.min(abs(flight_counts$n - flight_length))] segment_explore <- eagle_states %>% filter(flight_n == flight_n_explore) %>% arrange(stepend_dtime) %>% # number the fixes in the segment mutate(fix = row_number()) ``` ::: ## 2D plot (x-y) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = stepend_utme, y = stepend_utmn)) + geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(consensus)),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "UTM Easting", y = "UTM Northing", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png) ::: ::: ## Through time plots (x-time) ::: {.panel-tabset} ## Altitude ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # calculate the time in seconds from the first point in the segment segment_explore$seconds = segment_explore$stepend_dtime - segment_explore[[1,3]] ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = seconds, y = F_AOG)) + geom_point(aes(col = consensus),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Seconds in segment", y = "Altitude above ground (m)", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png) ::: ::: ## Speed ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = seconds, y = F_Sn)) + geom_line(aes(x=seconds, y=F_Sn), color = "grey") + geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(consensus)),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Seconds in segment", y = "Speed (m/s)", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png) ::: ::: ## Average speed ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = seconds, y = F_speed_mean_window)) + geom_line(aes(x=seconds, y=F_speed_mean_window), color = "grey") + geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(consensus)),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Seconds in segment", y = "Average speed for local window (m/s)", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png) ::: ::: ## Vertical rate ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = seconds, y = F_Vrate)) + geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), linetype="dashed") + geom_line(aes(x=seconds, y=F_Vrate), color = "grey") + geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(consensus)),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Seconds in segment", y = "Vertical rate (m/s)", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png) ::: ::: ## Average vertical rate ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = seconds, y = F_Vrate_mean_window)) + geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), linetype="dashed") + geom_line(aes(x=seconds, y=F_Vrate_mean_window), color = "grey") + geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(consensus)),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Seconds in segment", y = "Average vertical rate for local window (m/s)", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png) ::: ::: ## Turn angles ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = seconds, y = F_radians)) + geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), linetype="dashed") + geom_line(aes(x=seconds, y=F_radians), color = "grey") + geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(consensus)),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Seconds in segment", y = "Turn angles (radians)", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png) ::: ::: ## Cumulative turning angles ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = segment_explore, aes(x = seconds, y = F_turn_cum_window)) + geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), linetype="dashed") + geom_line(aes(x=seconds, y=F_turn_cum_window), color = "grey") + geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(consensus)),size=.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = consensus_colours) + labs(x = "Seconds in segment", y = "Cumulative turn angles for local window (m/s)", col = "Consensus state") + theme_light() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-28-1.png) ::: ::: ::: The states from each method through a single flight segment, with the consensus state at the bottom. We use the same flight segment as in the classification scripts (the one closest to 1500 fixes), and the same segment is shown in the map below. The whole segment is too dense to see clearly, so we only plot a window of 300 fixes (change `fix_window` to look at a different part of the segment). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # the first and last fix to plot fix_window <- c(1, 300) segment_explore %>% filter(fix >= fix_window[1], fix <= fix_window[2]) %>% select(fix, all_of(state_cols), consensus) %>% # one row for each fix and method (as characters, as the factor levels differ) pivot_longer(-fix, names_to = "method", values_to = "state", values_transform = as.character) %>% mutate(method = factor(c(method_labels, consensus = "Consensus")[method], levels = c(method_labels, "Consensus")), state = factor(state, levels = names(consensus_colours))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = fix, y = method, fill = state)) + geom_tile() + scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) + # put the first method at the top scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) + scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) + labs(x = "Fix number in the flight segment", y = NULL, fill = "State") + theme_bw() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](classification_agreement_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-29-1.png) ::: ::: # Data explorer with states and agreement The same data explorer as in the classification scripts, coloured by the agreement between methods, the consensus state, the states from each of the methods, the probability of the most likely HMM state, and some of the flight variables. Use the 'Colour by' dropdown to switch between them, and hover over a fix to see all of the values. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # the agreement and state variables, then the flight variables. # The first variable is the one shown when the map loads explore_vars <- c("agreement", "consensus", state_cols, "hmm3_prob", "F_AOG", "F_Sn", "F_Vrate", "F_radians_abs") # variables with negative and positive values get a diverging palette centred on 0 diverging_vars <- c("F_Vrate") # colours for the categorical variables (the same as in the plots above) map_colours <- list(agreement = agreement_colours, consensus = consensus_colours, kmeans_inst = state_colours, kmeans_agg = state_colours, kmeans_comb = state_colours, hmm = state_colours, embc = state_colours) # the same function as in the classification scripts, with one addition - the # 'colours' argument, which sets the colours of categorical variables flight_explorer <- function(segment, vars, diverging = character(0), colours = list(), height = 650) { segment <- segment %>% arrange(stepend_dtime) n_fix <- nrow(segment) # hover labels - timestamp and the (unclipped) value of every variable label_rows <- map(vars, \(v) { val <- segment[[v]] val <- if (is.numeric(val)) as.character(round(val, 3)) else as.character(val) paste0("", v, "", "", val, "") }) labels <- paste0("", format(segment$stepend_dtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "", " (fix ", seq_len(n_fix), " of ", n_fix, ")", "", reduce(label_rows, paste0), "
") %>% map(htmltools::HTML) # colour palette for each variable make_palette <- function(x, v) { if (!is.numeric(x)) { okabe_ito <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#999999") # keep the levels of factors (so states missing from this segment don't shift the colours) if (!is.factor(x)) x <- factor(x) # use the colours given for this variable, otherwise the Okabe-Ito palette cols <- if (v %in% names(colours)) colours[[v]][levels(x)] else okabe_ito[seq_along(levels(x))] pal <- colorFactor(cols, domain = NULL, levels = levels(x)) return(list(pal = pal, x = x)) } lims <- quantile(x, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE) if (v %in% diverging) { lims <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(lims)) pal <- colorNumeric("RdBu", domain = lims, reverse = TRUE) } else { pal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = lims) } list(pal = pal, x = pmin(pmax(x, lims[1]), lims[2])) # clip to the colour range } palettes <- map(set_names(vars), \(v) make_palette(segment[[v]], v)) # the point colours for each variable (switched in the browser by the dropdown) point_colours <- map(palettes, \(p) p$pal(p$x)) # a single layer of points (so the hover labels aren't duplicated for every variable) m <- leaflet(segment, height = height, width = "100%", options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>% addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>% addPolylines(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, color = "white", weight = 1, opacity = 0.6, group = "Flight path") %>% addCircleMarkers(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, radius = 4, stroke = FALSE, fillColor = point_colours[[1]], fillOpacity = 0.9, layerId = paste0("fix", seq_len(n_fix)), label = labels, labelOptions = labelOptions(textsize = "12px", direction = "auto")) # one legend per variable - only the selected one is shown for (v in vars) { m <- m %>% addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = palettes[[v]]$pal, values = palettes[[v]]$x, title = v, opacity = 1, className = paste0("info legend legend-var legend-", v)) } m %>% addLayersControl(overlayGroups = "Flight path", options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>% addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft") %>% # add a 'Colour by' dropdown that recolours the points and switches the legend htmlwidgets::onRender(" function(el, x, data) { var map = this; function colourBy(v) { var cols = data.cols[v]; for (var i = 1; i <= data.n; i++) { var m = map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix' + i); if (m) m.setStyle({fillColor: cols[i - 1]}); } el.querySelectorAll('.legend-var').forEach(function(l) { l.style.display = l.classList.contains('legend-' + v) ? '' : 'none'; }); } // leaflet only draws the layers once the map is visible (e.g. inside // a tab), so wait until the points exist before adding the dropdown function setup() { if (!map.layerManager || !map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix1')) { setTimeout(setup, 200); return; } addDropdown(); } setup(); function addDropdown() { var ctrl = L.control({position: 'topright'}); ctrl.onAdd = function() { var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'info legend'); div.innerHTML = 'Colour by
'; div.querySelector('select').addEventListener('change', function() { colourBy(this.value); }); L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div); L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div); return div; }; ctrl.addTo(map); colourBy(data.vars[0]); } }", data = list(vars = vars, cols = point_colours, n = n_fix)) } flight_explorer(segment_explore, explore_vars, diverging = diverging_vars, colours = map_colours) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
